evidence_summary: Randomized metastatic breast cancer study evaluated adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy in HER2-overexpressing tumors. The US label permits biomarker-selected use in defined breast cancer indications. The CIViC amplification profile requires appropriate HER2 assay context.

Randomized evidence in previously treated ALK-positive advanced NSCLC showed progression-free survival benefit versus chemotherapy. The US label supports metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC. This assessment is scoped to ALK fusion-positive NSCLC and does not rank competing ALK inhibitors.

LUX-Lung 3 tested first-line afatinib against chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma. L858R is a non-resistant sensitizing alteration covered in the metastatic NSCLC labeling context. Trial results from pooled common mutations do not estimate a variant-specific effect.

COMBI-v randomized patients with untreated BRAF V600E/K metastatic melanoma and showed improved survival for dabrafenib plus trametinib versus vemurafenib. The FDA labeling supports this combination in unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600E/K melanoma. The estimate pools V600E and V600K.

Pediatric midline high-grade astrocytoma sequencing identified recurrent somatic ACVR1 mutations. G328V can be supportive context in the CIViC disease setting. The cohort establishes recurrence and does not establish ACVR1 G328V alone as a defining criterion for H3 K27-altered disease.

Single-patient expanded-access evidence in adult Ph-like ALL with ETV6::NTRK3 demonstrated temporary cytoreduction. A single adult case gives limited durability and generalizability evidence. The tumor-agnostic solid tumor indication cannot be transferred to leukemia.
